solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The grain being bad, had a meeting about it

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the meeting word is wrapped around the word for bad

parts.note: met means had a meeting
ill means bad, as in ill luck

explanation.surface: A cereal crop has gone bad and a committee gathers to discuss it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The grain' at the front is the definition, not the subject of 'being bad'; 'about it' means round the word just given, so 'being' and 'it' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Millet is a small-seeded cereal crop grown for food and fodder.

clue.text: Factory people currently employed

definitions.note: said of the water channel, which is put to work as a current

parts.note: a mill is a factory, as in a cotton mill
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: A note on how many staff a works has on its payroll at present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'currently employed' looks like jobs at the factory; it means put to use as a current of water, which is what a mill's channel does.
explanation.definitionFit: A millrace is the channel of fast water used to drive a mill wheel, so its current is put to work.

clue.text: Slash dead tree at the core

indicators.note: at the core places the tree word in the middle of the word for dead

parts.note: late means dead, as in the late king
acer is the maple genus of trees

explanation.surface: Instructions to cut into the heart of a dead tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to tear or gash the flesh, a synonym of slash as a verb.

clue.text: They look and sound agreeable

indicators.note: sound tells you the word for agreeable is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: ayes are votes of agreement, so agreeable voices are ayes

explanation.surface: Some people both seem and come across as pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes are the organs we look with, so they are what does the looking.

clue.text: Double-crosser, jailed more than once?

definitions.meaning: an unfaithful lover who cheats on a partner
a two-time offender, one who has served time twice

explanation.surface: A traitor who has also seen the inside of a prison more than once.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cheats on a partner is said to two-time them; the second sense reads it as a repeat convict.

clue.text: Put a foot wrong and his job is to bail you out

definitions.text: Put a foot wrong and his job is to bail you out

parts.words: Put a foot wrong and his job is to bail you out
parts.note: in cricket a batsman who steps out of his crease can be stumped by the fielder behind the stumps knocking off the bails

explanation.surface: Sounds like a lawyer or friend who rescues you from trouble after a misstep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bail you out' looks like rescue; in cricket the bails are the small crosspieces on the stumps, and this fielder knocks them off to put out a batsman out of his ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket fielder behind the stumps stumps a batsman who strays from the crease by removing the bails.

clue.text: A word or a sentence

definitions.meaning: a word or expression with a set meaning
a prison ... is a sentence served

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson weighing a single word against a full sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Term means both a technical expression and a period of imprisonment.

clue.text: A girl gets assistance when males are around

indicators.note: the males are around, so they surround the help word

parts.note: men are males
aid means assistance

explanation.surface: A young woman finds help comes along whenever men are nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Maiden is an old word for a young unmarried woman, a girl.

clue.text: On first of September put up wager with gold sovereigns

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the turned pieces above the September letter
put up in a down clue means the wager and gold words, joined, are written upwards

parts.note: a lay is a bet, a wager
or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of September

explanation.surface: Someone bets gold coins at the start of September.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns LAY with OR, giving ROYAL. 'sovereigns' looks like gold coins, but it means monarchs.
explanation.definitionFit: Royals are kings and queens, and sovereigns are monarchs.

clue.text: Plant put right outside the church

indicators.note: put works with outside: the right is placed around the church
outside means surrounding, so the legal-right word wraps round the church

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold another's property until a debt is paid
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A gardener sets a plant correctly just outside the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put right' reads as correct, but 'right' alone is LIEN, a legal right to retain goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Lichen is a simple organism growing on rocks and walls, loosely called a plant.

clue.text: Shortage of transport in southern metropolis

indicators.note: in puts the transport word within the southern city

parts.note: a metropolis is a big city
a car is a means of transport

explanation.surface: A complaint about too few buses and trains in a city in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarcity is a lack or insufficiency of something, a shortage.

clue.text: They don't seem to mind life being a continuous drag

definitions.text: They don't seem to mind life being a continuous drag

parts.words: They don't seem to mind life being a continuous drag
parts.note: a drag is a pull on a cigarette, and those who light one from the last take continuous drags

explanation.walkthrough: 'drag' looks like a tedious bore; it is a puff on a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: People who light one cigarette straight after another are puffing almost without a break.

clue.text: It's unusual to return right on time

indicators.note: on places the right letter next to the turned time word
return means the time word is read backwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Coming back on schedule is a rare event.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare means seldom seen or found, so uncommon or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: What he does is appropriate

parts.note: appropriate as a verb means take for oneself, to steal

explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' reads as an adjective meaning fitting; it is the verb meaning to take what is not yours.
explanation.definitionFit: A robber appropriates, that is steals, other people's property.

clue.text: Kent port trade

definitions.meaning: A coastal town in Kent, a county in south-east England

explanation.surface: Commerce in a harbour town in the south of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kent town shares its name with the verb meaning to do business in goods.

clue.text: Time to leave the cloth?

parts.note: to leave something to someone is to bequeath it in a will

explanation.surface: Is it time for a priest to give up holy orders?
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cloth' suggests the clergy; here it is just fabric. 'leave' is the noun-like sense in a will, a bequest.
explanation.definitionFit: Twill is a fabric woven with diagonal ribs, such as denim.

clue.text: Be under professional scrutiny

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the be letters below the professional word

parts.note: pro is short for professional
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being examined closely by an expert.
explanation.definitionFit: A probe is a thorough investigation, close scrutiny of something.

clue.text: The best parts of old wireless sets

definitions.meaning: the ... is an idiom for the very best
a fine wire touching a crystal in early crystal radio sets

explanation.surface: The finest components from vintage radios.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for something excellent and also the name of a fine wire used in crystal radio receivers.

clue.text: On the verge of alarming changes

indicators.note: changes says the letters of alarming are rearranged

explanation.surface: Close to some worrying alterations.
explanation.definitionFit: Marginal means at the edge or border, on the verge.

clue.text: Possibly, I am not afraid to speak

parts.note: to dare is to be bold enough, not afraid
to say is to speak

explanation.surface: Maybe; but I'm brave enough to voice my opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a way of conceding something is likely or perhaps true.

clue.text: Dressing table used to cover a rough wall?

definitions.text: used to cover a rough wall?

parts.note: a plaster is a dressing for a wound
a board is a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A bandage and a dressing table being used to hide a bad wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Plasterboard is a panel of gypsum between paper sheets, fixed over walls to give a smooth surface.

clue.text: Country where rabies is unusual

indicators.note: is unusual says the letters of rabies are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A nation where the disease is seldom seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Serbia is a Balkan nation with Belgrade as its capital.

clue.text: One may play it — and one may get licked

definitions.meaning: a brass instrument like a small trumpet
an ice-cream cone, also called by this name in Britain

explanation.surface: A musician might play it, but one might also be beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a brass instrument and an ice-cream wafer cone.

clue.text: Wild rose — the symbol of love

indicators.note: wild says the letters of rose run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A wild rose as the emblem of romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, whose statue in Piccadilly Circus is a famous love emblem.

clue.text: A hundred and one in debt shrink in fear

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
one who owes is an ower

explanation.surface: A hundred people in debt recoil in terror.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower is to crouch or flinch back in fear.

clue.text: I depart right after the operatic prince

parts.note: to go is to depart

explanation.surface: I leave right after the opera's royal hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link word here, not an ordering signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Igor is the title hero of Borodin's opera.

clue.text: One who draws level?

definitions.meaning: a person who ties a game, read as tie-er
a layer or rank, as in a wedding cake's layers

explanation.surface: Someone who catches up with the leader in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draws level' suggests catching up; split it into one who draws, a tie-er, and a level.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a row or layer, and read as tie-er it is one who draws a match.

clue.text: I'm a leader of Muslims

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: leader of takes the opening letter of Muslims

explanation.surface: A cleric introducing himself as head of a Muslim congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads prayers in a mosque and so is a leader among Muslims.

clue.text: Rubbish holder in container- ship?

parts.note: a bin is a container
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: Is the rubbish carried on a container ship?
explanation.walkthrough: 'container-ship' looks like one vessel; split it into container and ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A bin liner is a plastic bag lining a waste bin to hold the rubbish.

clue.text: Corrects the final part in a script

indicators.note: in places the final part within the letters for a script

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a script
the end is the final part

explanation.surface: An editor rewrites the closing section of a screenplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to alter something to correct or improve it.

clue.text: Star skater is knocked out

indicators.note: knocked out says the letters of skater is are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A star of the ice rink is concussed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' looks like a celebrity skater; it is the printed symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An asterisk is the star-shaped printing mark.

clue.text: Take on recruit

definitions.meaning: to hire someone for a job
to enlist a new member of staff

explanation.definitionFit: To employ is to give someone work, which is both hiring and enlisting staff.
